sources_considered.why: Dated benchmark results distinguish baseline LLMs from a program-generating approach.
Controlled syntactic generalization research supplies context about both successes and variation between models.
The later June benchmark report supplies more specific measurements; the launch essay also contains broader interpretations that are not measurements.
Relevant abstract-reasoning research, but its experiments span revisions beginning in 2023 and their execution dates are not separately established.

evidence_items.locator: New High Scores section and accompanying score table
evidence_items.explanation: Semi-private verification scores were 14% for Claude 3.5, 5% for GPT-4o and 4.5% for Gemini 1.5, supporting a substantial abstraction-task weakness. A GPT-4o system generating and refining Python programs reached 43%, showing useful progress while also changing the system being evaluated.

The study finds that generalization varies with training data and supervision, with code-trained models performing better. The research was initially reported in 2023, so it is context rather than decisive evidence within the chosen observation period.

unresolved_gaps: Low performance on ARC does not establish that all available neural methods lack sufficiently general abstractions.
The record does not supply a representative cross-domain test that distinguishes inadequate generality from successful but limited abstraction.
Marcus supplies no threshold for the breadth or reliability required.
